textures.name: Sandy Soil
textures.physical_feel: Gritty, rough, does not stick together when wet, particles visible to the naked eye
textures.ribbon_test: Cannot form a ball or ribbon; falls apart immediately when squeezed
textures.aeration: Excessive aeration; roots breathe easily but dry out rapidly
textures.nutrient_leaching: High leaching vulnerability for nitrogen and potassium
textures.management_guidelines: Incorporate organic matter, farmyard manure (FYM), and use frequent light irrigations or drip.

textures.name: Clayey Soil / Heavy Black Cotton Soil
textures.physical_feel: Very sticky, smooth and plastic when wet; forms hard clods with deep fissures and cracks when dry
textures.ribbon_test: Forms a shiny, flexible ribbon longer than 5 cm without breaking
textures.moisture_retention: Extremely High (can retain water for many days)
textures.aeration: Poor when wet; risk of root hypoxia / asphyxiation if waterlogged
textures.nutrient_leaching: Very Low; high cation exchange capacity (CEC)
textures.management_guidelines: Provide field drainage channels. Avoid cultivating when too wet (prevents compaction). Ideal for conserving post-monsoon moisture for Rabi crops.

textures.name: Loamy Soil
textures.physical_feel: Even, mellow blend of sand, silt, and clay. Slightly gritty yet pliable, soft to the touch
textures.ribbon_test: Forms a firm ball and a short ribbon of 2.5 to 3.5 cm before breaking
textures.moisture_retention: Optimal; holds moisture without becoming waterlogged
textures.aeration: Excellent pore space balance for healthy microbial activity and root respiration
textures.management_guidelines: The benchmark agricultural soil. Maintain organic carbon levels through crop rotation and green manuring.

textures.name: Silty Soil
textures.physical_feel: Silky, flour-like, talcum powder texture when dry; slippery and soapy when wet, not sticky
textures.ribbon_test: Forms a weak ribbon of 1.5 to 2.5 cm that flakes easily
textures.aeration: Moderate, susceptible to surface crusting under heavy rain
textures.management_guidelines: Prevent soil crusting by mulching. Enhance structure with organic compost.

textures.name: Mixed / Gravelly Loam
textures.physical_feel: Heterogeneous mixture of coarse sand, gravel, and loamy fines common on rolling Deccan terrain
textures.ribbon_test: Variable, breaks irregularly around small pebbles
textures.management_guidelines: Contour bunding and stone terracing help retain fine topsoil.

textures.name: Unknown / Unspecified
textures.management_guidelines: Conduct the simple 2-minute finger feel or jar sedimentation test documented in the Soil Identification Guide.

colors.name: Red Soil
colors.indicator_meaning: Rich in oxidized iron compounds (hematite). Common in Eastern and Southern Dry Zones (Alfisols). Typically light to medium textured, well-drained, acidic to neutral.
colors.caution: Colour is an indicator of mineral composition and drainage state, not an exact chemical measurement of NPK or pH.

colors.name: Reddish Brown
colors.indicator_meaning: Transition soil with moderate organic matter and iron oxides. Good general fertility and balanced structure.
colors.caution: Colour is an indicator of mineral composition, not an exact chemical measurement.

colors.name: Dark Black / Regur
colors.indicator_meaning: Vertisols rich in montmorillonite clay. High swelling and shrinkage characteristics. Typical of Northern Karnataka basalt plains. Holds high residual moisture.
colors.caution: Dark colour in tropical Vertisols stems from clay-titanium humus complexes, not solely organic matter.

colors.name: Brown Soil
colors.indicator_meaning: Medium textured soils with balanced organic matter. Common in river valleys and transitional plateau regions.

colors.name: Yellowish Soil
colors.indicator_meaning: Hydrated ferric oxides (limonite). Often found in lower slope positions or areas with intermittent high water table.

colors.name: Grey Soil
colors.indicator_meaning: Common in low-lying depressions or areas experiencing prolonged wetness (gleying). High silt or reduced iron.
colors.caution: Check for drainage issues before selecting waterlogging-sensitive crops.

colors.name: Light Sandy / Pale
colors.indicator_meaning: Coarse quartz sand with low iron and organic content. Very fast draining.

colors.name: Mixed Color
colors.indicator_meaning: Patches of red, brown, and gravel common in undulating Deccan terrain.

drainage_options.description: Rainwater disappears into soil within minutes. Typical of sandy and gravelly soils.
Water infiltrates steadily without pooling for long. Ideal for most field crops.
Water stands in puddles for 3 to 12 hours after heavy shower before soaking in.

drainage_options.id: Water remains for one or more days
drainage_options.description: Water stagnates for 24 hours or longer, creating squishy wet ground or standing pools.

moisture_retention_options.description: Surface becomes completely dry and dusty within 1 to 2 sunny days after rain.

moisture_retention_options.id: Soil retains moisture for a short period
moisture_retention_options.description: Stays damp for 3 to 5 days before drying.

moisture_retention_options.id: Soil retains moisture for several days
moisture_retention_options.description: Holds workable dampness for a week or more; cracks appear slowly.

depth_options.description: Less than 25 cm before striking rock, gravel, or hard pan. Restricts taproot development.
25 to 75 cm depth of workable soil. Suitable for most annual field crops.
Greater than 75 cm depth. Allows deep rooting crops (Sugarcane, Cotton, Red Gram, Fruit trees) to thrive.
